{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the big left-facing fish and split it into four strokes so all four of us could build at once from the first minute. I laid the start domino and the back stroke, which is the spine of the run. That stroke is connected to the start and carries the fall into the body. The fish outline is large, fills most of the table, and reads clearly as a fish. A single push knocks over about 105 of the 120 standing dominoes.

Execution: I worked steadily along the back and kept it connected as it grew. I used close inspections to find where the fall was stalling, mainly at the tail notch and the right edge. I tried several fixes there, and when they didn't catch I stopped touching the tail so I wouldn't knock over what was already standing. I then confirmed that everything was upright before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout, with regular updates on how far the run had reached and when each teammate could start their stroke. I made sure each person knew what they owned and when to begin. I asked for hands-off time around the spots I was working on to avoid bumps, and I took on board teammates' suggestions about how the curve should sweep. I agreed with the table's decision to stop adjusting near the end.

Leadership: I set the direction in the first seconds with a clear concept, a stroke plan and named owners. That let the table start building immediately. I kept the timeline visible, calling out when a stroke was ready for the next person. I also made the call to stop changes near the deadline so the table finished with a stable, recognizable picture.", "my_share_percent": 35}
